headings.title: Introduction to Female Sexual Dysfunction
headings.content: Female sexual dysfunction (FSD) encompasses a broad range of recurring difficulties experienced during any phase of the sexual response cycle, resulting in personal distress for the individual. For a condition to be clinically recognized, these symptoms must persist for a minimum of six months and cause significant interpersonal or psychological strain. In many Nigerian healthcare settings, discussing sexual health remains heavily stigmatized due to cultural and religious beliefs. Consequently, patients rarely volunteer these symptoms spontaneously during routine clinical encounters. Recognizing FSD as a legitimate health concern requiring professional intervention is the first step toward comprehensive holistic nursing care.

headings.title: The Female Sexual Response Cycle
headings.content:
Understanding the physiological stages of sexual response provides a baseline for identifying where disruptions occur. Masters and Johnson outlined the linear model, while later models incorporate emotional intimacy and circular feedback loops, which are particularly relevant for women.

- **Desire (Appetite)**: Psychological drive or libido fueled by hormones, fantasies, and emotional readiness.
- **Arousal (Excitement)**: Vasocongestion of pelvic tissues, vaginal lubrication, and clitoral engorgement.
- **Orgasm**: Rhythmic contractions of the pelvic musculature accompanied by intense physical and psychological release.
- **Resolution**: Return of the genital and systemic systems to an unaroused baseline state, often accompanied by a sense of well-being.

headings.title: Classifications and Types of Female Sexual Dysfunctions
headings.content:
Clinical classification systems divide female sexual dysfunctions into four distinct categories based on the affected phase of the response cycle.

| Category | Primary Clinical Feature |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Female Sexual Interest/Arousal Disorder** | Absence or reduction of sexual fantasies, urge, or receptive responsiveness. |
| **Female Orgasmic Disorder** | Marked delay, infrequency, or absence of orgasm, or substantially reduced intensity of orgasmic sensations. |
| **Genito-Pelvic Pain/Penetration Disorder** | Persistent difficulties with vaginal penetration, vulvovaginal pain during intercourse, or pelvic floor muscle tension. |
| **Substance/Medication-Induced** | Sexual dysfunction directly attributable to pharmacological agents or toxic substances. |

headings.title: Etiology and Predisposing Risk Factors
headings.content: Sexual dysfunction rarely stems from a single isolated cause; instead, it arises from a complex interplay of biological, psychological, and sociocultural factors. Biologically, hormonal fluctuations during the postpartum period, lactation, or menopause drastically reduce estrogen levels, leading to atrophic vaginitis and dryness. Chronic medical conditions such as diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and neurological disorders impair pelvic blood flow and nerve innervation. Psychologically, anxiety, depression, history of sexual trauma, and body image dissatisfaction heavily interfere with arousal. Sociocultural stressors, including marital conflict, financial strain, and religious guilt, further compound these vulnerabilities.

headings.title: Nursing Assessment and History Taking
headings.content: Conducting a comprehensive sexual history requires a non-judgmental, private environment that builds patient trust. Nurses should use screening questions that normalize the discussion, such as inquiring whether a patient has any concerns regarding their sexual well-being. The PLISSIT model serves as a practical framework, guiding the nurse from giving Permission (P) to providing Limited Information (LI), specific suggestions (SS), and intensive therapy (IT) referrals. The history must explore the onset, duration, and severity of the problem, distinguishing between lifelong and acquired dysfunctions, as well as situational versus generalized occurrences.

headings.title: Diagnostic Evaluation and Screening Tools
headings.content: Evaluating female sexual dysfunction involves a multidisciplinary approach combining clinical history, physical examinations, and validated screening questionnaires. Validated tools like the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) help quantify symptoms across multiple domains including desire, arousal, lubrication, orgasm, satisfaction, and pain. The physical examination includes a pelvic assessment to inspect for atrophic changes, pelvic organ prolapse, infection, or localized tenderness of the vestibular glands. Laboratory investigations may include fasting blood glucose, lipid profiles, and hormone panels to rule out underlying systemic pathology.

headings.title: Nursing Management and Therapeutic Interventions
headings.content: Interventions for female sexual dysfunction are tailored to the identified underlying etiology and may involve medical, surgical, or lifestyle modifications. For estrogen-deficient atrophic vaginitis, topical vaginal estrogen creams or moisturizers restore tissue elasticity and reduce dyspareunia. Lubricants and pelvic floor physical therapy, including Kegel exercises and biofeedback, help manage penetration disorders by improving muscle relaxation and control. When medications such as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors are identified as the causative agent, collaborating with the physician to adjust the prescription can alleviate side effects.

headings.title: Patient Counseling and Psychosocial Support
headings.content: Because sexual health is deeply intertwined with emotional well-being and interpersonal dynamics, counseling is a cornerstone of recovery. Nurses facilitate communication between partners, encouraging couples to explore non-coital intimate activities that reduce performance anxiety. Psychoeducation helps dispel unrealistic expectations fueled by media portrayals of sexuality. When psychological trauma, severe depression, or deep-seated marital discord exists, timely referral to specialized sex therapists or clinical psychologists ensures comprehensive rehabilitation.
